title: Twin runs: the current system and an AI-first Claude agent on one problem at the same time, everything from both captured side by side
request: Use the Claude API in chat instead of the OpenAI model, in all workflow phases, in the important decisions and in the solution draft chat, at the same time and concurrently with the current workflow: see how Claude solves the problem as an AI-first agent and how the current system handles it, see the differences, and capture and store everything from both approaches (sessions, chats, the agents' replies and logs, workflow runs, the decision samples) in a separate folder, organised and easy to find. R&D only.
spec: A twin run: one seed (a studied sample, a project, or a draft's chat), two lanes in two threads, each a complete workspace folder under <workspace>/twin/<run>/: the workflow lane is the current system (the intern's standard plan, the validator, no model), the AI-first lane is Claude as the agent with the same tools, task and validator, Claude also serving the stage notes, the leakage reviewer and the roles; every file each lane writes stays in its folder, the AI-first lane's every model request and answer verbatim; compare.json and COMPARE.md; a CLI that sends nothing without --yes; never the main workspace, never the sealed benchmark.
plan: Read the gateway (tiers, ChatClient, Bound, installed(), context.using), shadow mode (why it cannot carry a twin), the intern (start/run, _Model, the standard plan), the Home agent, the role advisors and their gating, the live harness (how it isolates a run), and the workspace layout.

Reach Claude through Anthropic's OpenAI-compatible endpoint with the studio's own ChatClient, so the gateway changes nothing; a ClaudeClient in the gateway's shape that keeps every exchange, writes the usage rows through Gateway.record, and stops at a request cap and a euro cap.

A Lane: its own ProjectStore, DraftStore, SessionStore, FileTraces, audit path (so the decision samples follow), a Services object with the lane's gateway for context.using; seeds from a sample, a project (table copied and registered again, suggestion and labels kept, stages left behind) and a draft (turns replayed); run_project with the intern, run_draft with the Home agent; a summary read back from the files.

run(): both lanes in threads, the engine's profile and the roles' gate set once around both; compare.json and COMPARE.md; run.json and README.md; a CLI with run, list, compare and samples; tests with a scripted Claude that drives the real tools and overrides a stage.
Review by a fresh reader; fix what it found; docs, the plan's A6.6 row, CLAUDE.md, README.

decisions.decision: Claude through Anthropic's OpenAI-compatible endpoint with the studio's ChatClient, not a native Messages transport.
decisions.why: The runtime appends the OpenAI-format assistant message verbatim and the tools are OpenAI-format; the compatible endpoint takes both, so no second transport and no gateway change for an R&D feature. A native transport can come when something the compatible endpoint lacks is needed.

decisions.decision: A separate lane per side, each a whole workspace folder, instead of the gateway's shadow mode.
decisions.why: A shadow only sees the served model's conversation and never acts; the AI-first side must run its own workflow with its own project. Shadow mode is also limited to local tiers by design, because its requests are outside every budget.

decisions.decision: The AI-first lane is the intern with a Claude client and the same tools, not a new agent.
decisions.why: The same tools, task and validator make the comparison about the decisions, not the harness; the moves, traces, audit and decision samples come for free.

decisions.decision: The transcript keeps the model's words whole but runs tool results through the trace's scrub, unless --capture-cells.
decisions.why: The reviewer showed describe_data's three example values per column reaching the transcript; the trace's CELL_KEYS scrub already exists for exactly that, so it is reused rather than a new mechanism; the session file still holds them, as the product's own sessions do, and the guide says so.

decisions.decision: An agent's approval or override is a decision label of its own source, agent.
decisions.why: A6.5 dropped agent approvals so they would never pass for a person's; the twin needs the agent's choice beside the rule's. A source of its own keeps both: the export's label field stays human-only.

decisions.decision: The engine's bundle cache gets a lock and keeps a few entries instead of one.
decisions.why: Two lanes preparing at once evicted each other's bundle on every stage and could race on a check-then-use; the cache now holds up to four, one per project running at a time.

decisions.decision: The engine's profile and the roles' gate are set once around both lanes, in the main thread.
decisions.why: Both are process-wide; set per lane, the first lane to finish would restore the full profile under the other, and the comparison would not be like for like.

decisions.decision: A twin run refuses a database workspace, a private source project (unless allowed) and any live model under DCLAB_NO_LIVE_MODELS, inside run(), not only in the CLI.
decisions.why: Each lane must be a folder of its own; a private project's names and previews must not reach a model by a twin's back door; a script calling run() gets the same guards as the CLI.

change: dclab_rnd/twin/ (claude.py: ClaudeClient, TwinGateway, NoModels, Transcript; lane.py: Lane, seeds, run_project, run_draft, summary, run_both; compare.py; __init__.py: run, list_runs, compare_run, README; __main__.py), dclab_rnd/studio/engine.py (bundle cache lock and size), dclab_rnd/decisions/labels.py and schema.py (agent label source), tests/test_twin.py, docs/guides/TWIN_RUNS.md, AGENTIC_FOUNDATION_PLAN A6.6, DECISION_SAMPLES.md, CLAUDE.md, README.

findings.defect: The scripted AI-first agent approved the data stage after run_all and lost every later stage.
findings.scenario: run_all, then approve_stage data: approve clears every later stage that is not pending, so leakage to final were gone and the later approvals returned errors; the lane still ended completed.
findings.cause: The engine's approval clears downstream results by design; the agent's order was wrong, not the engine.
findings.fix: The scripted agent runs and approves stage by stage, the order a careful agent takes; the comparison now shows the override it makes on the models stage.
findings.impact: None in the product; a lesson for the real Claude's task text, which now says to approve each stage after running it.

findings.defect: Every move in the comparison read as refused.
findings.scenario: The summary took transitions' allowed field as the verdict; it is the list of moves allowed next, and the verdict is status.
findings.cause: A misread of the transition entry.
findings.fix: The summary reads status, and the sequence names the stage of each move.

findings.defect: fast_profile() was entered per lane, and it is one global for the process.
findings.scenario: The workflow lane finishes first and restores the full profile while the AI-first lane is on its models and final stages: the lanes are no longer like for like, and a slow machine can push the AI-first lane past its minutes.
findings.cause: A process-wide setting treated as a per-lane one.
findings.fix: The profile is set once in run(), around both lanes.
findings.test: test_twin (both lanes complete under one profile)
findings.impact: Timing and even choices not comparable between lanes.

findings.defect: The engine's bundle cache was a one-entry dict with an unlocked check-then-use.
findings.scenario: Lane A sees its key in the cache, lane B clears the cache, lane A reads its entry: KeyError, the stage tool errors, the lane ends half-run. Without the race, each lane evicts the other's bundle on every stage.
findings.cause: The cache was written for one project at a time.
findings.fix: A lock around the cache and up to four entries, the oldest evicted.
findings.test: the engine tests and test_twin run both lanes at once
findings.impact: A rare failed lane; slower lanes.
alternatives: serialising prepare() across lanes (would hide the concurrency the twin is for)

findings.defect: The docs claimed the seven roles run on Claude; the product's gating kept most of them off.
findings.scenario: roles.on() reads DCLAB_ROLES and roles_judged.json, where only the feature engineer and the reporter are on, so the AI-first lane's understand_problem ran the rules alone.
findings.cause: The gating is the product's, not the lane's.
findings.fix: run() sets DCLAB_ROLES to every role for the run (the workflow lane has no model, so it is untouched), --roles judged keeps the product's gating, and run.json records which roles were on.
findings.impact: A comparison that was not what the docs said.

findings.defect: Tool results carried three example cell values per column into the transcript, and the docs said the files held only column names.
findings.scenario: describe_data returns examples per column; the intern feeds them back as a tool message; the transcript wrote the messages verbatim.
findings.fix: Tool messages go through the trace's scrub unless --capture-cells; the guide says what the session file still holds.
findings.impact: Cell values in a research file the docs described as free of them.
alternatives: capture-cells on by default (rejected: the product's own trace strips them)

findings.defect: A private project could be seeded into a twin and its names and previews sent to Claude; a script could call run() under DCLAB_NO_LIVE_MODELS.
findings.scenario: seed_project copied settings but dropped private; TwinGateway answers every purpose; only the CLI checked the environment.
findings.cause: The guards lived in the CLI.
findings.fix: run() refuses a private source unless allow_private, refuses a live transport under DCLAB_NO_LIVE_MODELS, and refuses a database workspace (a lane must be a folder of its own).
findings.impact: A back door past the product's privacy flag.

findings.defect: A draft lane whose model failed or was capped reported completed with the standard questions, indistinguishable from Claude's.
findings.scenario: HomeAgent.reply falls back to script_turn on any provider error and sets agent.model_note; the summary did not read it.
findings.cause: The fallback is silent by design in the product.
findings.fix: The summary and COMPARE.md carry model_note and the transcript's refusal count.
findings.impact: A misleading comparison after a cap.

measurements.name: a twin run on heart_disease with a scripted Claude (quick profile, 2 CPUs)
measurements.gate: both lanes complete; the comparison shows the override; the main workspace untouched
measurements.result: both completed in about 16 s together; workflow 5 tool calls (describe, propose, set, run_all, export), ai_first 16 (stage by stage with approvals and one override); models stage extra_trees vs logistic_regression, final extra_trees_baseline vs logistic_regression_C01; holdout ROC-AUC compared; 0 refused moves
limits: a scripted agent, not Claude: it proves the harness, not Claude's judgment

measurements.name: the request cap
measurements.gate: the AI-first lane is refused at the cap and the run still finishes with a comparison
measurements.result: 3 requests sent, the fourth refused and recorded, workflow completed, COMPARE.md written

measurements.name: tests
measurements.gate: test_twin, test_decision_samples, test_studio, test_intern*, test_draft_flow, test_agents* pass
measurements.result: see the commit: run on the build machine
limits: no live Claude request was made: the endpoint and model name are from Anthropic's documentation, to be confirmed by the first real run

outcome: One command runs a problem through the current system and through Claude as an AI-first agent at the same time, keeps everything each did in its own folder, and writes a comparison; the first real run needs only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and --yes.
lessons: A process-wide setting (a profile, an environment gate, a one-entry cache) must be set once around concurrent lanes, never inside each.
Reuse the product's own scrub for anything written verbatim: the trace already knew which keys carry cells.
Guards belong in the function a script calls, not only in the CLI around it.
risks: No live request to Anthropic was made on this machine: the OpenAI-compatible endpoint's behaviour with this runtime's tool format is to be confirmed by the first real run (--max-requests 5 first).
The AI-first lane's sessions hold cell examples as the product's sessions do; a run on a confidential table stays on the machine that made it.
Comparisons are one run each on one holdout: differences inside the intervals are noise; repeat runs before drawing a conclusion.
